- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.7) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >3% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +2% above peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤-0.5) mid-period, model frequently underestimates; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% to counteract mean reversion bias.
- Model exhibits strong lag in reacting to sentiment shifts — if sentiment flips from negative to positive, delay 1–2 days before adjusting forecast upward.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently underestimates true price volatility; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to smooth out extremes; use median of recent 5-day window as anchor for correction.
